# Uploading Artwork to Manually Created Jobs

When you create an order by hand, for example at the counter or from an email, its jobs have no artwork yet. You can upload the customer's files straight into each job, check that the copies match the quantity ordered, and send the job to production.

---

## Before you start

Manual artwork uploads need two things set up first.

### 1. Storage must be set up

The files are kept in your S3 storage, so storage has to be connected first.

1. Go to **Settings → My Store → Storage**.
2. Under **1. Choose your storage**, choose **Pixfizz storage** (most labs) or **My own Amazon S3**.
3. Finish the remaining steps until your bucket is saved and the connection test passes.
   * Note: the switches under **Features** stay unavailable until storage is ready.

### 2. Turn on Manual Artwork Uploads

1. In the same Storage page, scroll to **4. Features** (or **3. Features** if you use your own Amazon S3).
2. Turn on **Manual Artwork Uploads**.
3. Confirm the **Enable Manual Artwork Uploads?** message.
   * Note: this is not the same as **File Uploads**. **File Uploads** covers files that customers send you. **Manual Artwork Uploads** covers files your staff add to jobs.

![Manual Artwork Turned ON](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/29a69af7-56fe-4018-b018-cce9cb766b0e.png)

### 3. Make sure the product's process allows the right file types

The files you can upload depend on the **process** linked to the product's category.

1. Open the process and find **Allowed File Types for Manual Artwork Upload**.
2. Tick the file types you accept, for example JPG/JPEG for photo prints, or PDF for printed documents.
   * Note: files of any other type are rejected when you upload. If the category has no process, assign one first (see *Assigning Pixfizz Categories to Production Processes*).

---

## Uploading artwork

1. Open the order and find the job.
2. Click the upload button on the job row to open **Upload Artwork**.
3. Check the job summary at the top. It shows the product (for example 4x6" Photo Print), the **Quantity ordered**, and the file types you can upload.
4. Click **Choose files**, or drag files onto the box marked **Drag and drop files here, or choose from your computer**.
5. If you need to, set the **Artwork type** and the **Default quantity for new files**, then change the **Copies** for each file.
6. Keep an eye on the counters: **Uploaded copies**, **This batch** and **Files selected**. They show how far you are from the quantity ordered.
7. Upload the files.

![Upload Manual Artwork](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/14337352-144a-4a64-ad09-4d0410cdbb84.png)

### After uploading

Once the files are uploaded you'll see **Artwork uploaded** and three choices:

| Choice | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add more files** | Upload another batch to the same job |
| **Send to Production** | Release the job to production now |
| **Done** | Close the window and leave the job as it is |

* Note: if the copies don't match the quantity ordered, you'll see **Quantity does not match the order**. Choose **Go back** to fix it, or **Continue to Production** to send it anyway.

![Continue Uploading or Send to Production](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/09f5bac3-b278-48ef-a05b-1ef7ae581d69.png)

### Viewing or removing files

Open the job and go to its **Artwork** section. From there you can preview, download or delete each file. Deleting a file also lowers the copy count, so you can upload a replacement.

---

## Cleaning up old artwork

To keep storage costs down, you can have manually uploaded files deleted automatically once a job is finished.

1. Go to **Settings → My Store → Storage → Features → Manual Artwork S3 Cleanup**.
2. Make sure the switch is on. It turns on automatically at **30** days when you turn on Manual Artwork Uploads.
3. Change **Days after job completed** if you want a different number, then click **Save Cleanup Settings**.
4. To clean up straight away, click **Run Cleanup Now**. It shows you what would be removed, then asks you to confirm with **Delete files**.

Good to know:
* The countdown starts when the job is **completed**, not when the file was uploaded.
* Artwork delivered by Pixfizz is never removed, and open or cancelled jobs are never touched.
* The file stays listed on the job with the label **File removed by cleanup**, so you keep the history.

---

## Summary of Best Practices

* Connect storage and turn on **Manual Artwork Uploads** before you take orders by hand.
* Set the allowed file types on each process so staff can't upload the wrong format.
* Check that **Uploaded copies** matches **Quantity ordered** before choosing **Send to Production**.
* Leave cleanup on unless you need to keep artwork for longer.
